Self-paced course provider

Study.com

Current offer. College Saver covers a general-education selection; College Saver Pro adds premium and upper-division options. Study-help and test-prep subscriptions are different products.

Research profile · confirm exact school and course acceptance

How the credit works

ACE or NCCRS recommendations for eligible courses under a credit-earning membership.

Pace and learning format

Self-paced. Current plans advertise unlimited monthly completions, with two concurrent Saver courses or three concurrent Pro courses.

Costs to check

Published plans: College Saver $95/month and College Saver Pro $235/month. Confirm course inclusion and current checkout terms.

Check the current checkout terms and the costs that apply to your actual course list. Membership time, assessments, materials, retakes, transcripts, and school fees may need separate attention.

Assessments and requirements

Current official support describes required final exams as open-book and non-proctored. Course-specific assignments still apply.

Before you commit

  • Choose the exact receiving school, degree, and catalog year.
  • Confirm this specific course, recommendation or transcript source—not only the provider’s name.
  • Ask which requirement the learning will satisfy and check duplicate-credit, grade, date, and source limits.
  • Keep a written school decision before paying for an outside course you need for graduation.

Official sources

  • Study.com official website
  • Current credit-earning plans
  • Required membership and current exam model
  • Open-book College Saver finals

Catalog review date: 2026-11-01. Confirm current terms with the provider and receiving school.

Put the source inside a degree plan.
